newsitem.title: CHINA: China says in talks with Iraq to produce oil.
newsitem.headline: China says in talks with Iraq to produce oil.

text.p: China said on Monday it was holding talks with Iraq on the possibility of signing "massive" oil exploration contracts.
The official Xinhua news agency said that discussions between China National Petroleum Corporation and Iraq included plans for the production of five million tonnes of oil a year.
The two sides are also discussing a plan for China to help Iraq develop an oilfield with annual capacity of 15 million tonnes, Xinhua said. It gave no further details.
Chinese sources had said previously that talks were being held to cooperate on seismic studies and exploration.
China, once a net oil exporter, has been forced to import increasing amounts of oil and oil products to meet demand from a rapidly expanding domestic economy.

Under a stalled oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations, Iraq would be allowed to export $2 billion of oil over renewable six-month periods to buy badly needed food and medicine to ease the effects of international sanctions.
The sanctions were imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
Xinhua also quoted oil industry specialists as saying that China was planning to import more oil products. It gave no details but this is largely in line with market expectations.
But the news agency quoted State Planning Commission official Li Xunli as saying that there was no problem for China to be self-sufficient in oil by relying on its own resources until 2010.
The report noted, however, that high water content had made it increasingly difficult to maintain high yields in the country's existing onshore oilfields.
China's older onshore production areas -- such as the big Daqing field in the northeast -- require costly tertiary production methods, such as water injection techniques.
As a result China is pinning its hopes on cooperation with foreign companies to develop new onshore fields in the far western region of Xinjiang and offshore.
Chinese offshore oil output is expected to hit 14 million tonnes this year, the news agency said.

Xinhua also noted the previously reported signing of a $400 million deal by China to build oil facilities in Kuwait and plans by Saudi Arabia to cooperate with China to set up oil refineries in the eastern Chinese province of Shandong.
Chinese firms were looking to conclude prospecting deals in the United Arab Emirates and elsewhere in the Gulf, Xinhua said.

China and Russia have agreed to jointly explore natural gas resources in Siberia and lay an oil pipeline from Siberia to China, Xinhua said. It gave no further information on the previously announced plan.
China was involved in prospecting in Canada, Papua New Guinea, Peru, Sudan and Thailand, the agency said without giving further details.
